text.en: Without water, the world cannot go on, as even an ancient saying warns.

This prose lesson on water begins by calling nature the greatest gift to living things: tall mountains, forests, green meadows, water bodies, fields and groves. It says it is our duty to use these wisely and protect them for the next generation, and so it speaks of water management (நீர் மேலாண்மை).
The lesson shows that ancient Tamils built tanks, canals and dams and valued water. Today water is scarce, so conserving and managing it is a public duty.
Terms: நீர் மேலாண்மை (water management), நீர்நிலை (water body), இயற்கை (nature) and பாதுகாப்பு (protection). The title echoes a line of Thirukkural, which says that the world cannot exist without water.
